Goldman Sachs.reason: Known by name, but Wall Street is mostly business-major territory here.

Harriet Tubman.reason: Fresh from school history lessons; young progressive crowd admires her.

Savannah Guthrie.reason: Morning TV host; undergrads barely watch network TV.

Today.reason: Known brand, but network morning shows are their parents' thing.

Norah O'Donnell.reason: Network news anchor few college students could name.

CBS This Morning.reason: Renamed, older-skewing morning show; off this room's radar.

Jake Tapper.reason: Politics-junkie students know him; most of the room doesn't.

CNN.reason: Everyone knows CNN, but cable news viewership skews old.

Rachel McAdams.reason: Mean Girls and The Notebook keep her beloved by young women.

Mark Ruffalo.reason: The Hulk; MCU made him familiar and liked by young adults.

Liev Schreiber.reason: Ray Donovan star; most undergrads couldn't place his face.

Spotlight.reason: 2015 prestige drama from their childhood; some film students know it.

Star Wars.reason: Universal pop culture; the sequels and Disney+ kept it alive for them.

BuzzFeed.reason: Faded millennial brand; they know quizzes and Unsolved, not the newsroom.

The Washington Post.reason: Known legacy paper, but students rarely read or subscribe.

Kendall Jenner.reason: Kardashian-Jenner fame and Instagram dominance hit this age group squarely.

Twitter.reason: Now X, but they know it and still use it for buzz.

Facebook.reason: They know it but see it as their aunt's platform.

swaps.name: Hamilton
swaps.why: The same cash slang built on the face of a banknote (the $10 bill), and this room knows Hamilton from the musical.

Harriet Tubman.note: Measured through the Hamilton musical film, which is how this crowd knows the name; the line loses the newly-announced-$20 angle, which has faded anyway.
